headline: Record foreign buying meets a hawkish Fed; Mahanadi Coalfields IPO opens

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Thursday, the nineteenth of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, foreign money is pouring into Indian shares at a pace never seen before. Foreign institutional investors have bought more than one lakh crore rupees of Indian stocks so far this month, the biggest monthly inflow on record. And Goldman Sachs has upgraded India to overweight.

Second, the global mood has turned cautious. Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's last meeting show almost all officials expect more rate hikes. The dollar firmed, gold slumped to its lowest in more than a year, and GIFT Nifty points to a weaker start here.

Third, Mahanadi Coalfields, the Coal India arm, opens its IPO of nearly 9,000 crore rupees today, after raising 2,295 crore rupees from anchor investors.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed on Wednesday. Profit booking ended a two-day winning streak. The Sensex fell about 500 points, or 0.61 percent. The Nifty lost 159 points, or 0.63 percent, to close at 25,228. That was the Nifty's biggest single-day fall this month, and it trims November's gain to 9.4 percent. Bank Nifty ended at 62,038, close to its record high.

Consumer durables took the worst hit, down over 3 percent, with Titan and Kalyan Jewellers cracking 5 percent as gold prices fell. Metals lost nearly two and a half percent. Gold loan lenders Muthoot Finance and Manappuram slipped nearly 4 percent, on worries about the value of the gold they hold as collateral.

On flows, the numbers are striking. Foreign investors have put in somewhere between 9.6 and 10.6 billion dollars this month, depending on the count. That beats the previous record of 8.4 billion dollars from December 2020, and it comes after they pulled out a net 2.95 lakh crore rupees in the first ten months of the year. Domestic institutions have gone the other way, selling around 55,500 crore rupees so far this month. Analysts quoted by Business Standard expect steady mutual fund inflows to turn them back into buyers.

Goldman Sachs has upgraded India to overweight, with a Nifty target of 28,500 by the end of 2027, citing improving earnings.

The rupee gave up its seven-month high and closed flat at 93.44 to the dollar.

The levels to watch: analysts see support for the Nifty at 25,000, and then 24,800. On the way up, resistance sits in the 25,400 to 25,500 zone. GIFT Nifty was near 25,160 early this morning, pointing to a lower open.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
To the primary market. Mahanadi Coalfields opens today and closes on Monday, the twenty-third. The issue is worth 8,981 crore rupees, priced between 129 and 136 rupees a share, with a lot of 110 shares. LIC led the anchor book. The grey market premium has cooled to around 3 rupees, down from recent highs.

Crystal Crop Protection was subscribed 1.15 times on its first day, led by employees and retail investors, with a grey market premium of around 18 rupees. And Bengaluru realty developer Assetz has SEBI's nod for its IPO, reportedly to raise about 1,200 crore rupees.

In the block deal window, Fairfax India sold IIFL Finance shares worth 3,488 crore rupees to around 40 buyers, including Nippon India and SBI Mutual Fund. And Kotak Mutual Fund, BlackRock and others bought Groww shares worth 1,905 crore rupees.

Two corporate actions to note. SpiceJet's board has approved raising up to 5,500 crore rupees, as dues, salary delays and flight disruptions strain its finances; the stock has hit the upper circuit for six sessions. And Dalmia Bharat's board meets on the twenty-third to consider a share buyback, with no size or price disclosed yet.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
A short results roundup. Public sector banks have posted their highest ever half-year profit. Net profit for April to September rose about 17 percent to around 1.1 lakh crore rupees. Their total business crossed 300 lakh crore rupees, gross bad loans fell to a record low of 1.69 percent, and the capital adequacy ratio improved to 16.89 percent.

On the other side, Relaxo Footwears fell 6 percent after disappointing September quarter numbers, and is down 11 percent in four sessions. Glass Wall Systems rose 4 percent on a new order, after reporting a 31 percent rise in quarterly profit.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, and a story that matters for every equity investor. The government is reportedly reviewing a proposal to halve the securities transaction tax on cash equity trades, while raising levies on derivatives to curb speculation. A cut in long-term capital gains tax is also under consideration. The recommendations go to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman ahead of Budget 2027.

On growth, economists polled expect the economy grew around 7.6 percent in the July to September quarter. ICRA is a little lower at 7.5 percent, which would be a five-quarter low.

On rates, Goldman Sachs expects the Reserve Bank to raise rates by a total of 75 basis points by the middle of next year, taking the repo rate to 6.25 percent. It sees inflation staying above 6 percent into early 2027, and growth easing to 7.2 percent.

Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran struck a different note. He said India may have to manage rupee strength, not weakness, next financial year, as several agencies expect Brent to fall below 80 dollars a barrel.

On trade, exports grew 16.6 percent in the first half, and Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal says India is on track for its target of one trillion dollars this year. He also expects gold imports to fall to 35 to 40 billion dollars this year, from about 72 billion last year, after import duty was raised to 15 percent in May.

Two quick ones. Rabi sowing is down 11.3 percent, with wheat acreage down 15 percent, as post-monsoon rain ran 34 percent below normal. And one for practising professionals: SEBI says merchant bankers must register as valuers with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board to keep doing valuations under the Income Tax Act and foreign exchange rules.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, the Fed is the story. Minutes of its last meeting show almost all officials expect more rate increases, and Fed governor Christopher Waller backed aggressive action. The dollar index is up nearly 2 percent this month. Gold tumbled more than 3 percent overnight to a fourteen-month low, and silver fell even harder, pushing the gold to silver ratio above 82.

Oil is holding firm, with Brent near 92 to 93 dollars a barrel. Kotak Neo says the war premium has faded, but lingering risks keep 90 dollars intact. Further out, Goldman Sachs sees Brent easing to 78 dollars by December 2027, as the market moves into a surplus.

In technology, Nvidia's quarterly revenue and profit more than doubled, and its forecast of 130 billion dollars beat estimates. But the stock gave up an early gain of almost 3 percent, as uncertainty over its leadership lingers. And Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, priced its IPO at 83 dollars a share, above its targeted range. Reports say the offering could raise around 90 billion dollars and value the company near 1.4 trillion dollars, setting up what may be the biggest market debut ever. Asian markets are mixed this morning.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India and US trade deal you're following. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday that the legal texts are almost final. But he said the signing may take time, because it depends on Washington settling its new tariff rules and its ongoing Section 301 investigations.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now to your money. If you hold the Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series Two, the Reserve Bank has announced its premature redemption price. Investors stand to gain around 191 percent if they bought offline, and about 194 percent online, before interest.

A useful consumer ruling from Telangana. The state consumer commission held that a UPI PIN alone does not prove a customer agreed to a transaction. It ordered SBI to refund 55,000 rupees lost in a fraud, plus 30,000 rupees as compensation and costs.

Two tax and labour rulings. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal at Jaipur condoned a 105-day delay in filing an appeal, after a death in the family, and deleted a 20 percent disallowance of business expenses. And the Karnataka High Court has said employees who leave before five years should not assume they lose gratuity; their actual days worked and the Act's provisions must be checked.

For card holders, HDFC Bank is cutting reward points on income tax and GST payments made with its BizBlack Metal card by 40 percent, from the twenty-first of December.

And one date for your calendar: today is the last day to buy shares to qualify for dividends with a record date of tomorrow, Friday, from companies including Oil India and Ashok Leyland.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty holds 25,000 as global caution meets record foreign buying. Watch the first day of bidding for Mahanadi Coalfields, Anthropic's market debut in New York, and Dalmia Bharat's buyback meeting on Monday. Have a good day, and I'll be back tomorrow morning.
